answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small bond and earn reputation only through verified, useful work over time, like a dune that grows grain by grain rather than appearing overnight. A fresh identity starts with no trust, so an attacker spinning up thousands of clones at dawn gains nothing: each clone must separately stake funds and complete real tasks before it can vote or earn. Like yarrow spreading slowly through a field, trust accrues gradually and cannot be faked in bulk, making a mass fake-identity attack expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
